file_description: Historical Oil Wells (Pre-2009) - Monthly well count by status, extraction method, and concept code
data_format: LONG format - multiple rows per field-month, one per concept code and extraction method
priority: LOW - Historical data, useful for long-term trend analysis but not critical for recent operations
use_case: Historical well count trends, artificial lift evolution, operator consolidation history, field development patterns

field_descriptions.well_count: Number of wells in the specified status and extraction method category for the field-month. Integer count.
field_descriptions.status_concept_code: Numeric code (1-6) indicating well operational status. Code 1 = active production with specified lift method. Codes 2-6 = various inactive statuses with extraction_method = 'Parados' (shut-in).
field_descriptions.extraction_method: Artificial lift method for active wells (concept=1) or 'Parados' (shut-in) for inactive wells (concept=2-6)
field_descriptions.field_name: Field name (yacimiento) - note: no field_id in historical data, matching to modern data requires name matching
field_descriptions.data_date: Date stamp of data entry - end of month

status_concept_descriptions.active_production: Concept code 1 - Wells actively producing oil with specified artificial lift method or natural flow. Contributing to monthly production.
status_concept_descriptions.temporarily_shut_in: Concept code 2 - Wells temporarily shut in, capable of production but not currently flowing. Reasons: maintenance, equipment repair, market conditions.
status_concept_descriptions.remote_areas_no_infrastructure: Concept code 3 - Wells in remote areas lacking pipeline infrastructure or gathering facilities. Cannot deliver production to market despite being capable.
status_concept_descriptions.shut_in_reserve: Concept code 4 - Wells drilled and completed but held in reserve. Economic or strategic reasons. Not currently producing.
status_concept_descriptions.other_inactive_reasons: Concept code 5 - Wells inactive for unspecified reasons. May include regulatory restrictions, legal issues, technical problems, or pending decisions.
status_concept_descriptions.maintenance_or_issues: Concept code 6 - Wells under maintenance, workover, or experiencing equipment/operational issues. Expected to return to production.

extraction_method_descriptions.mechanical_pump: Sucker rod pump (beam pump) - most common artificial lift method historically. Surface unit drives subsurface pump via reciprocating rods. Suitable for low-medium rates, viscous oil.
extraction_method_descriptions.electric_submersible_pump_esp: ESP - electric motor-driven centrifugal pump installed downhole. High-volume lift, handles water. Typical: 500-5000 bpd.
extraction_method_descriptions.progressive_cavity_pump_pcp: PCP - positive displacement pump with helical rotor. Excellent for viscous oil, sand production. Handles 10-2000 bpd.
extraction_method_descriptions.gas_lift: Inject high-pressure gas into production tubing to lighten fluid column. Versatile, reliable, handles high volumes.
extraction_method_descriptions.natural_flow: Well flows naturally without artificial lift - reservoir pressure sufficient. Most economical but typically depletes over time.
extraction_method_descriptions.hydraulic_pump: Hydraulic-powered subsurface pump using power fluid circulation. Used where electric power unavailable. Less common than ESP or mechanical pump.
extraction_method_descriptions.plunger_lift: Free-traveling piston cycles through tubing to lift liquids. Used in gas wells with liquid loading. Intermittent flow, low maintenance.
extraction_method_descriptions.shut_in_not_applicable: 'Parados' - well is shut-in/stopped. No artificial lift system operating. Applies to concept codes 2-6.

unit_notes.well_count: Integer count of wells - not production volumes
unit_notes.aggregation: To get total active wells: sum all concept=1 across extraction methods. To get total wells: sum all concepts.
unit_notes.no_production_data: This file contains well counts only, not production volumes or rates

data_quality_notes.no_field_id: Historical data lacks field_id. Must match to modern data using field_name string matching. Field names may have changed 1999-2008.
data_quality_notes.company_name_changes: Company names reflect historical ownership. Many companies have merged, been acquired, or changed names since 1999-2008.
data_quality_notes.concept_code_interpretation: Concept codes 1-6 are numeric, not well-documented. Interpretation based on data patterns and extraction method correlations.
data_quality_notes.spelling_variations: Extraction method spellings may vary slightly (e.g., 'Prograsiva' vs 'Progresiva'). Standardize during translation.
data_quality_notes.zero_vs_null: Zero well count may mean: (1) no wells in that status, (2) field not active that month, (3) data not reported.
data_quality_notes.data_completeness: Pre-2009 data may have gaps. Data collection standards improved in later years.

calculated_metrics.total_active_wells: SUM(well_count) WHERE status_concept_code = 1 - total producing wells
calculated_metrics.total_inactive_wells: SUM(well_count) WHERE status_concept_code IN (2,3,4,5,6) - total non-producing wells
calculated_metrics.shutin_fraction: total_inactive_wells / total_well_count - indicates reliability issues if high
calculated_metrics.mechanical_pump_fraction: mechanical_pump_count / total_active_wells - indicates field maturity and depth
calculated_metrics.esp_fraction: esp_count / total_active_wells - indicates high water cut or high-rate production
calculated_metrics.natural_flow_fraction: natural_flow_count / total_active_wells - indicates young field or high reservoir pressure

technical_notes.historical_context: 1999-2008 was pre-Vaca Muerta era - all conventional production. Shale development began ~2010.
technical_notes.artificial_lift_evolution: Tracking lift method changes over time shows field maturity. New fields start with natural flow, transition to artificial lift as pressure depletes.
technical_notes.mechanical_pump_dominance: Mechanical pumps dominated Argentina conventional oil production 1999-2008. Still common today for mature fields.
technical_notes.esp_adoption: ESP adoption increased through 2000s as water cuts rose and higher rates needed. Now standard for high-volume wells.
technical_notes.data_vintage: This data is 15-25 years old. Well counts, lift methods, and operators have changed significantly.
technical_notes.inactive_well_costs: High inactive well counts (concepts 2-6) indicate high carrying costs and potential reactivation opportunities.
technical_notes.concept_code_limitation: Numeric codes less intuitive than descriptive status names in modern data. Translation aids interpretation.

data_integration.matching_challenge: No field_id in historical data. Must match to modern field database using field_name string matching with fuzzy logic.
data_integration.time_gap: This data ends at 2008. Modern well production data starts 2009. No overlap period for validation.
data_integration.use_for_trends: Best use: long-term artificial lift evolution, historical operator activity, well count growth 1999-2008.
data_integration.supplementary_only: Treat as supplementary historical context, not primary data source for current operations.

use_cases.artificial_lift_history: Track evolution of lift methods over time - natural flow to mechanical pump to ESP/PCP adoption
use_cases.field_maturity_analysis: High mechanical pump fraction indicates mature field. High natural flow fraction indicates young field or pressure maintenance success.
use_cases.operator_history: Track historical operator presence and consolidation patterns from 1999-2008
use_cases.shutin_trends: Historical shutin patterns may indicate chronic field issues or market dynamics
use_cases.limited_current_value: Low priority for current emissions/operations analysis - data too old

limitations.outdated: Data is 15-25 years old - operators, field names, well counts, and lift methods have changed significantly
limitations.no_field_id: Cannot directly join to modern data without name matching and validation
limitations.no_production_volumes: Well counts only - no production rates or volumes to weight by importance
limitations.no_well_ids: Cannot track individual wells - only aggregate counts by status and lift method
limitations.concept_codes_unclear: Numeric concept codes (2-6) not well-documented. Interpretation based on patterns.
limitations.low_priority: Low value for near-term operations, emissions estimation, or current field analysis

example_analysis.active_fraction_python: active = df[df['status_concept_code'] == 1]['well_count'].sum(); total = df['well_count'].sum(); fraction = active / total
example_analysis.field_name_matching_python: from fuzzywuzzy import fuzz; best_match = max(modern_fields, key=lambda x: fuzz.ratio(historical_name, x))
